notes: Source counting (coordinator rule): all GM/Chevrolet material (Heritage kits, brochures, dealer albums) = ONE source. Each fact needs 3 independent sources, at least 2 of them non-GM (NHRA, Chevy Hardcore, Wikipedia counted once across all its articles, Hagerty, Mac's Motor City Garage, EPA).

1958-1975 entries reuse verify_bel-air.json sources that cover the whole full-size line (GM kits/brochures, Chevy Hardcore 'Impala Engine Options' articles, Wikipedia engine articles); Wikipedia Bel Air citations were dropped and replaced with Wikipedia Impala citations.
1958: the Impala was a Bel Air sub-series; NHRA lists it as BEL AIR body '(Impala)'.
1976-1985 GM kits OCR'd/read from page images (1976-1979 full-line, 1980/1981/1983 'Impala', 1982/1984/1985 'Caprice' kits, all B-body Chevrolet). From 1983 the Impala was a sedan only.
1977-1985 Wikipedia citations are mostly generation-level (engine list), so they confirm availability, not the year's rating.
'nhra_plus_one' = NHRA plus one other independent source (short of the rule). Statuses: confirmed, three_sources_not_nhra, nhra_plus_one, two_sources_not_nhra, nhra_only, disputed, race_only.
HP: advertised gross through 1971, SAE net from 1972.
